result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the fear of difference. Not just tolerance, but a deep, unshakable belief that diversity—of thought, identity, culture, and experience—is the foundation of human progress. I’d dismantle the systems that pit people against each other based on arbitrary lines: borders, race, religion, or ideology. Instead, I’d foster a world where curiosity about "the other" is the default, where empathy isn’t a virtue but a reflex, and where collaboration is the only path forward.

This wouldn’t erase conflict entirely—difference will always challenge us—but it would reframe those challenges as opportunities to grow, not threats to fear. Imagine a world where no child is taught to hate, where no leader can weaponize division, where every person’s story is met with the same reverence as their own. That’s the world I’d fight for. Not because it’s easy, but because it’s the only one worth fighting for.
